lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: recognizing linear, quadratic, and exponential situations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

steps: It is the multiplier per year.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (3, -14) and (6, -23). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 8, 10, 12, 14. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.

items.prompt: A population of 800 grows by 12% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 4 years, to the nearest whole number.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 50 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
A stays ahead permanently because 50 is larger than 3.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2000(0.95)^t, with t in years. What does 2000 represent?
choices: the fraction of value retained each year, 0.95, meaning a 5% annual loss
the value of the asset when it was new, $2000
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the total value lost over the asset's life

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (4, -14) and (9, -24). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 14, 18, 22, 26. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 4.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 4.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A population of 2000 grows by 5% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 8 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 73 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 2, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 73 is larger than 2.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
